title: Liver elastography (FibroScan)
what: A machine uses ultrasound to measure how stiff your liver is. No needles and no radiation.
why: To find out if the liver has stiffened, which is called fibrosis: with hepatitis, fatty liver, frequent drinking, or changes in blood tests.
tell_doctor: If you have a pacemaker or another implanted device
If you recently had a hepatitis flare or drank a lot of alcohol. This can make the result too high

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 3 hours. After eating, the liver gets stiffer for a while. Check the exact time with your clinic.

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: A little plain water is usually fine.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, so you can easily uncover your right side.

bring: Past ultrasound, elastography, and liver test results
A tissue to wipe off the gel
steps: You put your right arm behind your head. This widens the gaps between your ribs
A little gel is put on your right side
The probe is placed between your ribs
The machine takes about 10 measurements. Lie still
feel: Each measurement feels like a light push or tap
after: The gel is wiped off, and you can eat right away
The result is usually given right away, as numbers
Your doctor will explain what the numbers mean

faq.q: Is FibroScan the same as a liver ultrasound?
faq.a: No. An ultrasound shows what the liver looks like. Elastography measures how stiff it is. They are often done together.

faq.q: Why do I need an empty stomach for FibroScan?
faq.a: After eating, the liver gets stiffer for a while, and the result may be too high. So it is usually 3 hours without food.

reminders.text: Liver elastography in 3 hours. Do not eat from now on. A little water is fine.
